classification.difficultyReason: Extract the gradient of the line, take its negative reciprocal, equate that value to the derivative and substitute into the curve to obtain the coordinates.

content.prompt: Find the coordinates of the point on $y=x^2-2x-3$, where the tangent is perpendicular to the line $x+4y-1=0$.

answer.short:
$(3,0)$

The given line has gradient $-\frac14$, so the tangent has gradient $4$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}4y&=-x+1\\y&=-\frac14x+\frac14\end{align*}$$

The line has gradient $-\frac14$. Perpendicular gradients have product $-1$, so the required tangent gradient is $4$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=2x-2\\2x-2&=4\\x&=3\\y&=3^2-2(3)-3\\y&=0\end{align*}$$

The point is $(3,0)$.
